chapter: Dancing schools, Sapiro and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Joining Sapiro's band at the Bamboo Inn
summary: He walked into the Chinese-restaurant nightclub and got the saxophone job, his first band with special arrangements; he lists sidemen including Joe Garland, Manzie Johnson, Jimmy Archey and Freddy Johnson, and the club soon folded.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: and a rhythm section, you know, so -- so I went up there one night. I was always scouting around with my nose in everything. I was working at the Dancing School then, with Willy Martineau, the parody, up at 116th Street. So during my travels I went around there -- I know why I went up there that night. My sister was going to business school up there on 134th Street somewhere, and I walked up there one night. So I said, "Let me go in this Bamboo Inn and see what's going on in there." It was a nice place in those days, and they served Chinese food, and there was a Chinese decor and everything, you know, and this band was playing so I went in -- somehow I got involved in there, and they were looking for a saxophone player. Anyway, I got the job and I left the Dancing School I was in after a year and a half and I went up there to work.
And that was again playing arrangements?
Well, that was really the first time that I played in a band that had a book with special arrangements.
Oh.
And they had one or two of Fletcher Henderson's arrangements.
Do you remember who else was in that band?
Oh, yes. Joe Garland. Who was the other saxophone player? Oh, Roy Eldridge's brother. What's
his name? Joe. Joe Eldridge. Manzje Johnson was the drummer. Ward Pinkeft. Langston Curl. Archey was the trombone player. You know Archy?
Jimmy Arche y.
Jimmy Arche y. Freddy Johnson was the piano player. In other words -- and I hadn't belonged to the union up till then. So I had to go join the union when I went up to that job.
So that was quite a band.
Oh, it was a heck of a band, sure. That was just the same as playing with Fletcher Henderson, you know, in a way of speaking.
Uh-huh.
Yeah, that was a real --
But he never -- Sapiro never became that well known.
No.
Let's turn this over.
- - - END T1 S1
What about Astik (PHONETIC) -- or am I skipping anything? Am I missing anything?

No, no, not really. No, you're not skipping anything. I -- oh, well what happened in this job, with Sapiro, I didn't work there long because it seemed as though the place folded or something. In fact I think it did fold.
The Bamboo Inn?
Yeah. Yeah. It -- so then they came --
Was that a big place?
Yeah, it was fairly large, yeah.
It served Chinese food?
